item.text: The workspace only contains the provided `test7.cpp` and the compiled reference binary, so I’m treating the library as fully black-box. Next I’m probing the executable with targeted inputs to reconstruct `ColorConverter::blend` and the exact output formatting.

I’ve confirmed the key CLI quirk: the C++ program never parses `b2`, and with 6 or more user-supplied values it treats the 6th value as `ratio` while the final argument is ignored. I’m now pinning down float formatting so the Rust output matches `std::cout` instead of just the math.

item.text: I’ve pinned the behavior far enough to start the Rust implementation: the blend is plain linear interpolation in `f32`, but the binary also relies on C++’s broken argument indexing and `std::cout`’s general float format. I’m validating the last formatting edge cases now so I can encode them directly instead of relying on Rust’s default float `Display`.

item.text:
Implemented the Rust migration as a complete Cargo project in [Cargo.toml](/output/Cargo.toml:1) with the entrypoint in [test7.rs](/output/test7.rs:1) and library modules in [src/cli.rs](/output/src/cli.rs:11), [src/color_space.rs](/output/src/color_space.rs:16), and [src/formatting.rs](/output/src/formatting.rs:14). The Rust code preserves the C++ behavior exactly, including the argument bug where `b2` is never parsed and the 6th user argument is treated as `ratio`, the literal `rgb1 * (1 - ratio) + rgb2 * ratio` blend formula, and `std::cout`-style float formatting including `nan`, `-nan`, `inf`, `-inf`, scientific thresholds, and signed zero.

Build artifacts are present at `/output/test7` from `rustc test7.rs -o test7` and `/output/target/release/test7` from `cargo build --release`. Verification passed with `cargo test`, direct edge-case comparisons against `/workspace/dataset/test7_executable`, and a 200-case randomized black-box comparison with no mismatches.
